task.description:
REWORK 1 of the ISS-0426 fix design. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR returned FAIL. Read its handoff (artifacts_in[0]) in full for the complete findings; this description states what must change to clear the gate.

BLOCKING DEFECT -- OQ-2 is a design gap, not implementation latitude. Your design's synchronous seam bypasses Task.yield on the nil-heap-words path only. But lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex:508-551 (run_with_heap_limit/5) carries its OWN hand-rolled wall-clock race: a bounded `receive ... after timeout_ms -> Process.exit(pid, :kill); {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, timeout_ms}}` built on :erlang.spawn_opt/2 instead of Task.Supervisor. ORCH has independently read executor.ex:508-551 and CONFIRMS the validator's finding: it is mechanistically the same race, and your seam does not address it. That leaves 4-5 call sites -- REQ-156 AC-1 (executor_test.exs:605), AC-2 (:644), and the heap-limited memory_result arms of the two mixed tests (:672, :910) -- still exposed to ISS-0426's exact failure mode after your fix ships. Your design's own section 7 defers this to ELIXIR-DEV; the gate's bar is 'unambiguous enough to build from', and a mechanism that does not know whether it covers 4 of its own Group 1 sites does not meet it.

RESOLVE OQ-2 AS A CONCRETE DESIGN ELEMENT. Decide and specify how the heap-limited Group 1 sites stop racing the wall clock. Note the constraint that makes this non-trivial and must be respected: run_with_heap_limit/5's max_heap_size enforcement REQUIRES a separate process (the heap limit is a spawn_opt on that process), so a naive 'call it synchronously in the test process' does not transfer from the run_script/3 case. Design section 5.3's ordering argument -- that a :killed DOWN is observed strictly before the `after` clause can fire, which is what lets :memory_limit_exceeded be distinguished from a caller-issued kill -- is load-bearing for REQ-156's correctness and must survive whatever you propose. Options you might weigh (none prescribed): a seam that spawns with the heap limit but waits unboundedly (no `after`), so the memory-limit path is still exercised while the wall-clock branch is unreachable; routing those sites to Group 2 instead and accepting tag-isolation for them; or something better. State the coverage consequence of whichever you choose -- specifically, what REQ-156 property each affected test still proves.

ALSO REQUIRED (both non-blocking on their own, but fix them in this pass):
  (i) Section 2.1's prose header claims '15 call sites across 10 tests', which is arithmetically wrong against your own table in the same section. The validator independently re-derived, from all 47 `test` declarations and all 31 `timeout_ms:` literals in the test file: 14 call sites across 11 tests for Group 1, and 11 Group-2-tagged tests (9 pure + 2 mixed) -- 22 tests total. Reconcile your prose to your table, using the count you can defend from the source.
  (ii) Point 1 asked you to weigh the alternatives to a new production seam -- a test-support module, a @compile-guarded definition, or simply making run_script/3 public-with-@doc-false. The validator judged the seam substantively SOUND and verified the build_script_error/3 precedent (executor.ex:438-457) is accurately cited, so this is not a demand to change the approach: it is a demand to show the comparison you made, so the choice is reasoned on the record rather than asserted.

UNCHANGED AND STILL BINDING: AC4 (no production timeout semantics changed, config/config.exs:17 untouched -- validator confirmed you are currently compliant, stay compliant); AC5 tag wiring mirroring :wasm_hang in both test_helper.exs and letflow.check.test.ex (validator confirmed CI genuinely reaches mix letflow.check.test via .github/workflows/ci.yml:126 -> mix letflow.check -> the mix.exs alias, so the tag approach is safe); the SCOPE BOUNDARY forbidding edits to the three wasm test files owned by the live run WF03-ISS0418-20260902; and the requirement that the fix be structurally verifiable rather than only statistically verifiable.

Design only -- still no implementation code. Update lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md in place. Complete this handoff and commit both to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902. rework_count is 1 of max 3.

result.summary:
OQ-2 RESOLVED as a concrete design element in a new design section 2.1.2 (previously just an open question deferred to ELIXIR-DEV). Root of the gap, confirmed by independently re-reading executor.ex:508-551 for this rework: run_with_heap_limit/5 has its own hand-rolled receive/after wall-clock race, mechanistically identical to Task.yield but built on :erlang.spawn_opt/2 + monitor instead of Task.Supervisor -- the prior revision's synchronous seam (section 2.1.1) only bypassed Task.yield on the nil-heap-words path and did nothing for this second mechanism.

Resolution: a second @doc false test-only seam, structurally mirroring run_with_heap_limit/5's own spawn/monitor/receive shape (spawn with max_heap_size, monitor, receive on {reply_ref, result} / {:DOWN,...,:killed} / {:DOWN,...,reason}) but with the after timeout_ms clause removed entirely -- an unbounded wait on the remaining three receive clauses only. Not 'remove the timeout and hope': max_heap_size: kill: true is enforced by the BEAM runtime on the spawned process regardless of whether anything is receive-ing for it, so heap enforcement itself is untouched; and design section 5.3's ordering argument (a :killed DOWN observed strictly before the after clause could fire, distinguishing memory_limit_exceeded from a caller-issued kill) is preserved and in fact strengthened to unconditional -- with no after clause at all, the caller issues no kill ever on this path, so every :killed DOWN this seam can possibly observe is unconditionally the BEAM's own doing, not timing-order-dependent disambiguation.

Coverage consequence stated per REQ-156 property per affected test in a new table (design section 2.1.2): REQ-156 AC-1 (line 605, 'smaller max_heap_words halts sooner') and AC-2 (line 644, '1GB alloc under 16MB limit fails cleanly') both keep proving exactly what they prove today -- neither asserts wallclock_timeout, both outcomes (memory_limit_exceeded or :ok) are BEAM-heap-kill-or-natural-completion, neither depends on caller patience. The two mixed tests' (656, 887) memory_result arms are noted as mechanistically identical and eligible in principle, but design section 2.4's existing, separately-stated choice (tag-isolate the whole test rather than split call mechanisms within one test body) is left as the authoritative treatment for those two arms -- not overridden, since that choice was already sound. run_with_heap_limit/5 itself, including its own after clause, stays completely unchanged; Group 2's own heap-limited test (line 788) keeps exercising that original after-clause branch exactly as today.

Reconciled counts: Group 1 is 14 call sites across 11 tests (not the prior revision's arithmetically-wrong '15 call sites across 10 tests' header, which contradicted its own table -- the table's row data was already correct, only the summary sentence undercounted by one test; matches CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's independently-derived count exactly). Of those 14, 11 call sites in 9 tests are nil-heap (section 2.1.1's seam) and 3 call sites in 2 tests (605 x2, 644 x1) are heap-limited (section 2.1.2's new seam). Group 2 remains 11 tagged tests (9 pure + 2 mixed), unchanged and already correct in the prior revision. Added a new 'Mechanism' column to section 2.1's table so the nil-heap/heap-limited split is visible in the table itself, not only in prose.

Also added the seam-alternatives comparison requested in point (ii): a new section 2.1.1a puts on record the comparison of (i) a new @doc false function on Executor (chosen -- directly precedented by build_script_error/3, smallest diff, keeps the existing execute_with_manifest/3-shaped call convention Group 1's tests already use) against (ii) a test-support module (rejected -- run_script/3 is defp, so a test-support module cannot call it without either collapsing back to option (i)/(iii) underneath it or duplicating REQ-154/155 rescue logic outside lib/, risking silent drift from production behavior) and (iii) making run_script/3 itself public-with-@doc-false (a legitimate close second, not chosen because its 3-arg already-normalized shape is a bigger behavioral-surface change than a same-shaped wrapper and would require restructuring each of the 14 call sites rather than a smaller drop-one-key edit -- but not prescribed away from ELIXIR-DEV if it proves simpler in practice). The validator had already judged the seam substantively sound and the build_script_error/3 precedent accurately cited, so this addition puts the reasoning on record without changing the chosen approach.

All four hard constraints re-verified against the updated design: AC4 unaffected (both seams additive, run_with_heap_limit/5's own after clause untouched, config/config.exs:17 still never referenced); AC5 tag wiring unaffected (OQ-2's fix is entirely inside executor.ex/executor_test.exs, doesn't touch the test_helper.exs/letflow.check.test.ex wiring the validator already confirmed CI reaches via ci.yml:126 -> mix letflow.check -> letflow.check.test); AC3 unaffected (both seams remove races rather than add them); Group 2 detection power unaffected (section 2.1.2 touches only Group 1's heap-limited sites, never any Group 2 test's assertions/workload/timeout value). Design sections 4 and 5 updated to cover both seams in the structural-verification checklist: confirm nil-heap rows call section 2.1.1's seam with no Task.yield in its body, AND heap-limited rows (605, 644) call section 2.1.2's seam with no after clause in its receive block -- both one-time diff/source reads, not repeated-run observations.

Also corrected the top-of-document scope statement, which inaccurately claimed lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex was 'explicitly out of scope, no production code change' even though both seams already lived in that file in the prior revision -- now states precisely that two additive @doc false test-only seams land in that file while every EXISTING function in it (execute_with_manifest/2,3, handle_yield_result/3, run_with_heap_limit/5's own after clause) stays byte-for-byte unchanged.
